text: Slit the throat, pay them off, scuttle in the shadows, or if all else fails, grovel-beg and shift the blame – always in that order!\\n– Skaven proverb
The frenzy of imminent triumph often slows its claiming: claws reach and rats bicker over future spoils before the vault is even open.
When properly supplied, the engineering den spits arcs of surging power, bathing the surroundings in spectacular – and 'semi-harmless' – viridescence.
Entire regiments of armed vermin on the cheap are a favoured courtesy of the rabble clans, who endlessly vie for the favour of their betters.
The clanrats have been sent under the impression that they are simply messengers... There is always more Skaven.
Whether the skirmish succeeds or not, the vampire will be occupied... And there is always more Skaven.
Arcane technology enraptures the mind and flesh-craft catches the eye, but theft and kidnapping remain the steadiest props of the Skaven economy.
When covering your tracks in quick-haste, remember: man-things are ever susceptible to the lure of unearned riches.
Observe their mouths drool-slaver and grubbing paws twitch-twitch... The man-things are as covetous as they are stupid!\\n– Whissk, Master-Pilferer
Advancement may be costly, yes-yes; how fortunate for the Underling then, that it can often be paid with the spoils of lesser vermin.
Twitching bodies, singed fur, charred rat-flesh: the unmistakable marks of Skaven progress!
A simple pox will not halt the genius of this plan – the Underling must eliminate this nuisance by any means necessary!
Gravity is for man-things to fear. "Reality" is for scaly-ones to keep. No self-respecting Skaven engineer feels bound by natural law.
Increased faith in the Great Horned One will surely help the Seer accomplish any task to the betterment of Skavendom and most importantly, Clan Scruten!
Your subordinates' incompetence will exact a terrible toll on your crafted machinations unless you act quick-quick, and – most displeasingly – allocate substantial resources.
The mishap has, for the time being, been smoothed over, and the expense will sit easier after flensing some vermin-scum's worthless hide.
Whispers carry word of treachery within your ranks. Unless cut out quick-quick, it will cripple your manoeuvres and expose the plan.
Your rivals' jealous attempts will never end, but for now the intricate webwork of your schemes has snared this perfidy.
The Underling's usage of tricks has drawn unwanted attention – harmless for now, but be careful of future Complications!
Your bumbling underling was ill-prepared for clandestine work; his crude actions have set the whole region on high alert!
Treachery! A rival Skaven clan has sent the guard straight towards your tunnels. Blame will come later; survival comes first.
Your underling has held a shrill debate over the plan’s details, proving his lack of discipline – and ensuring the foe has heard enough.
Unwise tests of the Underling's experiments have betrayed the plan with a blast loud enough to rouse Nagash by sheer force.
An experienced band of monster hunters has mistaken your tunnels for some beast’s lair. Their error will not make them less dangerous.
Whoever leads the region’s defence has caught the scent of your plan and now looks to stop it. Such competence is most offensive.
Your plan has drawn an Eshin contract. Some Skaven Lord has paid well to see it foiled – and perhaps to see *you* vanish with it.
A few rat warriors left tracks enough for a roaming patrol to follow. Their inept paws may yet cost you the whole scheme!
In a moment of peerless incompetence, your underling left the tunnels open for the local sentinels to explore...
A small party of hunters has caught your plan’s scent. They must be misled, butchered, or both – and quick-quick!
Desertion among the Skaven is only a crime if you get caught – or if those betrayed survive. Otherwise, it is the Horned One's wisdom applied.
Thievery is afoot in the Masterplan’s tunnels – and it is *your* coffers being pilfered, not the surface-dwellers’!
Clan Eshin is a terror between clans, yet its killers will reverse any Warlord’s fortune if he can outpay the rival who bought them first.
Secretive and highly trained they may be, but the black-clad assassins, too, are enterprising Skaven. With sufficient compensation, they are off your hide.
Endless ambition and pitiless savagery have placed the most infamous among the Warlord clans in your scheming path, with spiked flails and barbed shields supporting their argument.
With the same ruthless pragmatism that raised their upstart clan, the enforcers deem your contribution sufficient, and your plans no longer worth impeding.
Clan Moulder trades in horrors even Skaven find foul, but worse is the threat of withdrawing its lumbering brutes – unless an arrangement is made.
You were wise to part with spoils. Beastpacks sold to other clans are short on cunning; Master Moulders are not.

A veritable curse might be upon you, for a roiling, billious fug and the clattering of plague-censers herald the delirious fervour of the pestilent priesthood. Placate them however you can – or suffer!
Relieved as you are to see their bloated, sore-covered procession hobbling away, the putrefaction of their hollow eyes will surely accompany your dreams.
Its virulence – undeniable. Its origins – unknown. Plague has broken out in the tunnels, and Clanrats seem poised to flee in droves.

Beneath a banner of blood-red claw marks, a regiment of grim warriors appraise your pack with beady eyes, their jet-black fur bristling through gaps in jagged armour plates. They openly threaten usurping the plan!
The warp-moon surely glowers upon you today, for this pack of grizzled murderers would only leave once laden with unearned treasures and the promises of future favours.

Your machinations are in absolute accord with the will of the Great Horned Rat, so you cannot fathom how you provoked your sorcerous peers, nor what prompted their demands for tribute. Yet here they are!
Mentally, you hurl the ugliest execration at the smug horned sorcerer, and take small solace in the favourable omen of the brass bell tied to his belt. Doom... Doom... Doom...
A delegation of Warlock Engineers declares a trove of valuable contraptions as fault-prone at the most inopportune time. Unless, of course, a costly patch-job is done in the field...

Their greedy eyes remain hidden beneath the emerald sheen of arcane goggles, but the hint of a sneer by the chief engineer tells aplenty. You pray to the Horned One the nearest warp-relay vaporises him into fine dust.
Mutations from rats drenched in Warp-fuel are causing enough havoc to destabilise the plan!
The damage is done – the sound has likely alerted the entire continent, and the plan is hurtling towards failure as the Underling seeks a rat to blame.
Unwise tests of the Underling's experiments have betrayed the plan with a blast loud enough to rouse Nagash by sheer force.
Unwise tests of the Underling's experiments have betrayed the plan with a blast loud enough to rouse Nagash by sheer force.
The Underling's methods have yielded a positive result, but there is an audible warning that one of their devices may yet go off...
Sometimes, hiding is about weaving a sorcerous web of concealing shadow, intended to shroud the ratmen in utmost secrecy. More often, it means finding a crack in the wall large enough to cower in.

Any plan worth its salt takes full advantage of the Underway, for it branches off into a myriad different spyposts, minor fortifications, and secretive nest-dwellings that greatly increase its chances of success.
With the presence of strong Winds blowing across the region, your Underling will complete the plan with twice as more zeal!
A Warlock of Clan Skryre would never admit it, but such a success without detonation is not characteristic for Skaven tech.
When it does not backfire – killing its inventor in spectacularly grisly fashion – a Skaven apparatus is terrifying to behold.
When an Underling attempts to embezzle from the plan, it is not prudent to stop the thieving rat; instead, take a cut for yourself!
Higher in this subterranean hierarchy, the ruling Warlords and Grey Seers gorge themselves on warp-infused delicacies and victuals plundered from the surface realms.
Skaven shove and squeak in squirming mounds, tearing at morsels with feverish claws, for to pause in their frantic feast is to invite the starvation to claim their wretched souls.
A lucky find – someone has poorly attempted to hide their treasures, discovered even by an oft-incompetent Underling!
The teeming masses of slaves and Clanrats scramble in the muck for anything that glitters, coveting any trinket that would briefly elevate their miserable status.
A lucky find – someone has poorly attempted to hide their treasures, discovered even by an oft-incompetent Underling!
To scheming Warlords and canny engineers, every looted scrap of arcana, captured artillery, or curious machinery is a resource to be repurposed and fed into the greater Skaven war machine.
The teeming masses of slaves and Clanrats scramble in the muck for anything that glitters, coveting any trinket that would briefly elevate their miserable status.
By the Horned Rat's baleful eye! Boring a tunnel straight into the settlement's coffers and counting-houses offers a most efficient extraction route for this fleecing scheme.
Almost resembling a past mining operation, but left behind in a hurry – the Underling will happily take credit for obtaining it!
Even the smallest chunks of Warpstone are not to be dismissed, for they give off power indefinitely, and in their most compact form, fuel many of the Skaven devices to be somewhat portable.
Almost resembling a past mining operation, but left behind in a hurry – the Underling will happily take credit for obtaining it!
Greater quantities of Warpstone can be made more stable and safer to use after refinement – an elaborate process which only the most powerful of the baleful Skaven sorcerers can perform.
Even the smallest chunks of Warpstone are not to be dismissed, for they give off power indefinitely, and in their most compact form, fuel many of the Skaven devices to be somewhat portable.
The largest pieces of Warpstone plummet from the skies as meteors from the dark moon, and are tracked in their fiery descent by one of the hidden observatories scattered throughout the Old World.

The endless bickering and vying for resources is held in check by the silent death-squads of Clan Eshin. There is no use pointing paws as spies are everywhere, and it is perilous to plot against the plotters.
Rival Grey Seers and other assorted wizards will pay handsomely for trinkets with magic properties... and some of them are even genuine!
Rival Grey Seers and other assorted wizards will pay handsomely for trinkets with magic properties... and some of them are even genuine!
Rival Grey Seers and other assorted wizards will pay handsomely for trinkets with magic properties... and some of them are even genuine!

Disciplined well beyond the verminous average, this excavation patrol tunnels to the surface, establishes a fighting perimeter, and dismantles the priceless chunks of Morskrit with ruthless efficiency.
Among the Skaven, any perceptible weakness is an invitation to be killed and eaten. Perceive it among a minor rabble clan, and it is an invitation to a veritable feast.
Occasionally, the verminous tides boil up on a particularly bountiful lair of the surface-dwellers, and the Skaven's frantic, incessant nature makes a scavenging grotesque of the spoils of war.
On occasions prophesied well in advance by the Seers, the Dark Moon disgorges shards of such prodigious size that they must be allocated among projects and clans to prevent an all-out war.
For the lesser, surface-dwelling races, it is hard to discern where science ends and magic begins. To a Warpstone-elevated Skaven mind, such a delineation never even occurs.
In their pursuit of a superb extraction and unparalleled refinement of the Horned One's precious lifeblood, the sorcerer-inventors build drills of superb extraction and appalling cost.
Rival Grey Seers and other assorted wizards will pay handsomely for trinkets with magic properties... and some of them are even genuine!

Eager to please their masters with a surplus of Warpstone, overzealous taskmasters ban chewing the stuff. The deprived rats succumb more easily to bouts of the Black Hunger, and the stockpiles suffer!
“Untutored handling of its raw form racks body and mind. Practised manipulation of its refined state empowers both. Curious, yes-yes, very curious…” – Grey Seer Kreaquill
Rival Grey Seers and other assorted wizards will pay handsomely for trinkets with magic properties... and some of them are even genuine!
Rival Grey Seers and other assorted wizards will pay handsomely for trinkets with magic properties... and some of them are even genuine!
The Underling's eyes are especially keen at noticing hiding places of wealth – and their paws are especially good at lifting it.
A smart-wise Underling knows to discard unnecessary fragments in favour of gathering the resources that really matter and prevent them from being blamed!
The irascibility of Skaven over food cannot be understated, for a vicious dispute over a meagre carcass erupts into utter mayhem, culminating in vindictive waste of carefully allocated provisions.
Overloaded provision carts chain-collapse in a thunderous heap, punctuated by the shrieks of grain-slaves crushed beneath an avalanche of black corn and moonseed.
Most cunning treachery! Deviously positioned fires engulf your stockpile, while the billowing smoke and noisome stench of charred Skaven delicacies betray your position.
A trail of brass, silver, and broken trinkets marks a hapless Skavenslave desertion. Robbery shows ambition; the ruckus shows stupidity.
A squad of vermin grovels for forgiveness: their eagerness matched only by incompetence. Their premature raid returns with near-worthless loot, and has alerted the foe to your presence!
Whoever chanced upon the convoy of slave-hulk drawn wagons and their treasure-laden coffers has left nothing but a pile of splinters, warped metal, and staked clanrat bodies for all to see.

Prolonged contact with Warpstone is inadvisable for all but the most powerful Skaven, but this has not deterred the occasional upstart from overexerting and ending up a screeching, rampaging, mutated pile of distended rat-flesh.
Sometimes, an inordinate investment of Warpstone in an incomprehensible engineering design pays off in spades. This time, however, the spades are necessary to scrape the engineers off the walls.
A careless acolyte has clearly overindulged in emerald dust and deemed it appropriate to relay the Horned One's whispered tidings in an incoherent, ear-splitting tirade.
In the totality of Skaven experience, the most common thread among successful schemes and stratagems is their expeditious execution.
As beings that exemplify boundless greed – among many other 'qualities' – vermin-kind never lets their inability to enjoy the spoils of war inhibit their drive to attain them.

It enhances the visions of the Grey Seers, fuels the fleshcraft of Moulder, strengthens the poxes of Pestilens, drives the ingenuity of Skryre. What it does for us, I'm not so sure-sure, but I still want it!\\n– Tchixx of Clan Eshin
A Hell Pit Abomination rises from the hidden lab, dripping with old grafts and fresh hunger, ready to devour according to plan.
Prototype Stormfiends, likely a secret of Clan Moulder, lurk ready with grinderfists and blind obedience. Waste them usefully.
A Doomwheel waits in the lab, half-charged and wholly unsafe. Aim it at the foe and pretend the rest was intended.
Elite Clan Eshin operatives emerge from the shadows, willing to serve for one battle – and one carefully counted fee.
A secret Clan Rictus operation lends black-furred Stormvermin to the battle. Their discipline is costly, but enjoyably brutal.
Death globes from Clan Skryre, likely hidden for experimentation, are now yours to hurl into the battle with appropriate disregard.
An impossibly clean tunnel-puncture reveals a fiendish cannon, untouched save for a burst warp-coolant tank and melted crew. Easily replaced.

To the surface-dwelling races, the urban planning of vermin-kind might seem incomprehensible, even downright dangerous. That, of course, is indicative of their lesser intellect. They simply cannot fathom the hidden utility of rickety scaffolding and tunnels that wind upon themselves!
Trinkets and baubles, discovered during Skaven digging – they can aid the effort of establishing tunnels for the Under-Empire!
Befitting their secretive nature, the ill-gotten spoils of the assassin clan are distributed without explanation – but you can be sure that it always works out to their advantage.
The master moulders of the flesh-craft clan are among the richest Skaven in existence, their opulence clearly evinced by their corpulent bodies and bottomless purses.
What tokens a Warlord clan deigns to throw your way are always slicked with blood and grime: the fruitful bounty of the violence, extortion, and subjugation of lesser beings.
Investments are a sign of an inordinate interest by the inventor clan in your pursuits, for much of their resources are funnelled back into their own questionable contraptions.
A taxing adjustment of ritual formulae may hurry a Verminlord through the veil – but surely the natural world will protest the warped presence with redoubled effort?

For thirteen days, the Grey Seers writhe in the alcoves of their temples – addled with Warpstone and delirious with portents of the Horned Rat. All this, to halt a massive remnant of the Chaos Moon and wrench it earthward...

By the Horned Rat's will, the gnawing affliction of the Skaven known as the Black Hunger shall be abated by nourishment of a most furtive and bleak provenance. Thus, his teeming children might hatch plans of greater malice.
By the Horned Rat's puissance, the verminous horde teems in ever-greater numbers! The chittering legions under your command gnash their teeth, eagerly anticipating the ruin they will soon inflict.
By the Horned Rat's musk, the decaying influence of rat-kind strengthens across this land, and the vestiges of civilisation wither before the presence of the ravening swarm.

Inch by inch, the warp-meteor grows closer, urged on by the ceaseless chanting of the Grey Seers. Occasionally, chunks of its sickly-green surface are wrenched free and plummet towards the planet – doubtlessly, a gift of encouragement from the Great Horned Rat!
This malodorous warp-bile is the plague monks' masterpiece, concocted with such corrosive potency that it could worm its way through the surface of a celestial entity and collapse it from within.
By way of precise warpstone overexposure, these vat-grown specimens have bulged to grotesque proportions – impractical for conventional warfare, but consummate beasts of burden for the warp chunks.
Using these massive navigational devices, the Warlock-Engineers ceaselessly monitor the shards of the Warp-moon and calculate the complex trajectories necessary to reach their pocked surfaces.
A furtive network of Eshin spies cast a complex web of whispers, diversions, and half-truths across the region, maintaining the much-needed shroud of secrecy over the Skaven operation.
Strange winds howl across the tunnels, carrying distant, mocking laughter – a troubling portent that the clanrats stray further from the ascension ordained by the Great Horned Rat.

[[i]]"Across an endless tunnel leading nowhere, cloying fumes waft and blackened moss spreads. Faintly, brass chains rattle in the distance – ever close-closer..."[[/i]]/n– Hissweep the Rattler, under the effects of Warpstone

Grown berserk under invisible influence, entire tunnels' worth of rats erupt in orgiastic violence – arteries gush under chiselled teeth, snouts glisten with viscera – and then all grows eerily still and noisome with offal-stench.
A sea of hollow-eyed rats shudders in droning incantation, their decaying jaws like grottoes leaking stringy pus.
Cruelty among rat-kind has taken on an otherworldly quality, as they plunge blades of differing serrations into the flesh of their weaker vermin, and call their agonised screeching 'music'.
Paranoid and frenzied, the rat-men divide into doom-squeakers who screech visions of a prismatic apocalypse and tight-snouted cabals digging furtive tunnels in strange, geometric patterns.
With abject horror, you sense this pestilent reaper studying you with unguarded malice, for there are none more malignant or more uncompromising than these infested terrors.
A deep sense of cosmic wrongness descends with the pall of jet-black darkness, and is replaced by a creeping dread – this formless, shifting horror knows no bounds in its slaying...
Emerging from a rolling umbra, the battle-tyrant appraises the battlefield with a bloodthirsty gaze, and its all-encompassing lust for carnage gnaws at your soul.
Amid fumes of purest Warpstone, the miasma of fragmented futures creeps, and all its facets point to your violent and untimely end.
Clouds of curling smoke snake their way into the guard-rats' lungs with near-intelligent malice, and black-clad shadows slip unnoticed amidst the ungodly racket.
Clanrats grow exceedingly vicious and violent. Bloodshed seems to be their only delight, and after picking them clean, they string the skulls of the fallen on belts or wear them as trinkets.

Shrieking, the vat-grown mutants collapse into quivering heaps, their bulging muscles contracting with crushing force onto their experimental bone structure. Too late, you realise: you have been sold unstable Rat Ogres!
Mangy-furred clanrats grow patchy with buboes, their lesioned flesh weeping filmy secretions. Yet the near-joyous contentment of the afflicted is the most repulsive sight of all.

Stormvermin are a notoriously greedy and self-serving bunch, and the black-furred enforcers of Clan Rictus are the worst of them all. Having decided a trove of spoils is rightfully theirs, they have left a trail of maimed and squealing rat-guards as proof.

Amid the squeals of dying rats, their flesh sloughing off in formless chunks, you make a bitter note that what a passing Skryre caravan sold you as 'refined Warpstone' is, very clearly, nothing of the sort.
Moderation is ill regarded among the Skaven, but their newfound indulgence in ravenous appetites and purposeless cruelty has crossed a threshold darker still.
The verminous horde is acting erratically, aimlessly digging spiralling tunnels and forming gibbering throngs that lash out for no discernible reason.
The veil-tear disgorges a teeming mass of dreadful beings whose depthless malice cannot discern conjurer from intended victim.
An aura of despair and pervasive rot oozes from this culler of civilisation; where it treads, bile seeps and life wilts with dreadful speed.
The air grows ashen and biting as hungering darkness manifests. In its presence, the world grows colourless and wan as it snuffs out light, then hope, then life itself.
By way of a ritual most secretive and brazen, your Underling will attempt to conjure a Verminlord – the most dire of the Horned One's children!
To summon a conglomerate evil, all Skavendom’s aspects must proliferate – theft, sabotage, and murder foremost among them.
Dark are the flesh-craft clan’s creations, and their brazen demands are growing darker still. None who use Hell Pit’s horrors dare question its depravities.
Woe betide those who earn the pestilent priesthood's ire, for from their depthless sockets they bore weeping sores upon the unfaithful.
Twisted are the Warlock Engineers’ minds, and infernal the devices birthed in their warpforges amid fevered clangour and Warpstone thrum.
The sinewed battle-tyrant emerges amid whorls of acrid smoke, welcomed by chittering tumult. In its presence, the vermin embolden and, by their awe, deepen their malevolence.

At the zenith of its triumphant appearance, pitiless lashes of black lightning scorch the earth. A webwork of charred grooves is left in their wake, marking where this fathomless evil has wounded reality.
By feverish warp-glow, acolytes of horned sorcery ceaselessly scribble the diabolical incantations required to entreat the most powerful of the Verminlords.
The dimensional veil thins beneath tempestuous Winds of Magic, their howling a dirge for a reality beset by such umbral majesty.
Beneath the obvious tunnels lies Eshin’s private web: forgotten cracks, murder-holes, and routes known only to those who never miss.
This rat will only be a liability, they will surely cause the plan to fail – better to profit from their death and remove a potential traitor in one fell swoop!
Dare not question the diseased ones' favour. Better to chant the Liturgus Infectus and stoke their unflinching zeal into unholy fervour.
The Underling deems better rat-fodder a worthy expense, lest a weak army bring dire consequences upon his own hide.
Unholy amalgams of Moulder fleshcraft and Skryre techno-sorcery, these hulking abominations bear grafts that spew vile, burning ooze.
The appearance of such a virulent relic is a mighty honour of the pestilent order, for these pox-bearing vessels are ancient beyond memory and precious few in number.
This living mountain of misshapen flesh requires an equally hideous quantity of sustenance.
Most foes flee this behemoth: a rippling tide of unnatural spasms, dragging itself forwards with surprising speed on limbs, grafts, and mechanical bits.
Leadership squabbles among the Skaven are regularly settled by butchery, and an armoured cadre of Stormvermin is ideal for such dirty work.
What possessed the Warlock Engineers to deem the unearthly devastation of a warp-beam insufficient, and therefore in need of enhancement?
Of all the teeming masses, only the slave-rat worker dregs surpass Clanrats in number and contempt.
The arming standards of a chittering war machine – utterly indifferent to the masses that fuel it – are predictably low, producing unsophisticated but crudely effective results.
The arming standards of a chittering war machine – utterly indifferent to the masses that fuel it – are predictably low, producing unsophisticated but crudely effective results.

Viciously hooked and deformed by rust and misuse, the simple armaments of the Clanrat masses inflict wounds that long outlast their wielders.
These furtive squads move in the shadows well in advance of the verminous ranks – capturing strategic positions, harassing the foe and luring hasty pursuits into nasty death-traps.
This hulking crossbreed is a pinnacle of Moulder flesh-weaving, blending the frantic nature of Skaven with an Ogre's might and somehow magnifying the desperate hunger of both races.
The already unenviable fate of the Skavenslaves takes a turn for the worse in Clan Pestilens, where they double as test subjects of the newest maladies and contagions.

The majority of the Under-Empire's population is made up of its lowest caste individuals – a teeming, short-lived, verminous mass that is bereft of any hope save a quick and (relatively) painless death.

Take caution-care with this globe, for in its murk coils a roiling fug that scalds flesh from bone and fills the lungs with pus.\\n– Phikk the Impurged, Master Engineer

Night raids, arson attacks, and befouled water supplies are favoured terror tactics of these clandestine death-masters.
Night raids, arson attacks, and befouled water supplies are favoured terror tactics of these clandestine death-masters.

A death-dealing apparatus of an almost too-Skaven design, this whirling abattoir marries a warpstone generator to serrated devastation.
A death-dealing apparatus of an almost too-Skaven design, this whirling abattoir marries a Warpstone generator to serrated devastation.
Though black-furred vermin often take the soldier’s path due to their size and brawn, some develop speed and reflex enough to become a subtler breed of death-dealer.

The warlord stiffened suddenly, his eyes widening in disbelief. Blood rose from his throat in a gurgling froth. A second assassin wrenched his dark, serrated blade from the warlord's back.\\n– an Eshin tale

Panicked retreat is wholesale preferable to facing these monstrous tunnel fighters, for the spinning cleaver blades adorning their extremities are too well suited to butchery in the enclosed spaces of the labyrinthine dark.
What was initially a utility-driven flesh-graft quickly proved its effectiveness on the battlefield – for if a tool tunnels with ease through rock, what chance could bone stand?
Warp-lightning wreathes the brute’s hulking mass, its limb-like arcs flailing with near-intelligent malevolence, turning all they touch to ash.
Look no further for proof that a Master Moulder's flesh-craft is not a crude pursuit of strength and size, and can breed all sorts of nightmarish amalgamations driven by ravening hunger.
Multiple snarling heads? Muscles bulging beyond practicality? Projecting discharge of corrosive bile? Who knows what months-long submersion in the warp-vats and some creative surgery might bring?
Multiple snarling heads? Muscles bulging beyond practicality? Projecting discharge of corrosive bile? Who knows what months-long submersion in the warp-vats and some creative surgery might bring?
The fragile spheres of glass lobbed by the globadier skirmishers are filled with Warpstone-fueled fumes that, once inhaled, cause the flesh of their unfortunate victim to slough off in ruin.

Displays of tactical acumen, anticipation of treachery, or simply unquestioning brutality are lavishly praised and rewarded by more cunning leaders, who grant access to armaments otherwise inaccessible to lower-ranking warriors.

Displays of tactical acumen, anticipation of treachery, or simply unquestioning brutality are lavishly praised and rewarded by more cunning leaders, who grant access to armaments otherwise inaccessible to lower-ranking warriors.

These foul and ingenious devices come in many shapes and sizes, but most can be summed up as 'a whirling, multi-barrelled death-dealer – as likely to decimate enemy ranks as to malfunction and shred its operators in a shower of shrapnel.'
Bedecked with three sets of eight-barrelled weapons, even a dim-witted Rat Ogre can take simple pleasure in the carnage, slobbering a laugh-like gurgle.
The slow-witted and rage-prone brute quickly engulfs the battlefield in thick curtains of green-black warpfire, soon devolving into a hellscape for all sides involved.
Chemical warfare is a horror all too Skaven, for no panoply can withstand the gaseous embrace of shattered vapour-globes, and no prayer can ward off the death-smoke curling into the lungs.

Much like the stone it was refined from, warpflame melts the skin and mutates the flesh – leaving a congealed biomass at best and a screaming, deformed cripple at worst. Spreading such devastation en masse is a terrifying prospect indeed.

Much like the stone it was refined from, warpflame melts the skin and mutates the flesh – leaving a congealed biomass at best and a screaming, deformed cripple at worst. Spreading such devastation en masse is a terrifying prospect indeed.

Displays of tactical acumen, anticipation of treachery, or simply unquestioning brutality are lavishly praised and rewarded by more cunning leaders, who grant access to armaments otherwise inaccessible to lower-ranking warriors.
These devices marry great drills with warp energies, vaporising broken debris – or broken bodies – as the machine bores onward.

The rune-etched barrel of this fiendishly clever contraption is built to withstand the concentrated energy of an enormous hunk of Warpstone, directing it as a singular, destructive beam that eats away at matter with unearthly voracity.
Dwarf Engineers would never admit that in their rat-fiend way, Skaven Warlock Engineers perfected their handgun design, capable of punching through armour forged by the surface-dwelling races.
Dwarf Engineers would never admit that in their rat-fiend way, Skaven Warlock Engineers perfected their handgun design, capable of punching through armour forged by the surface-dwelling races.
It is not uncommon for a Grey Seer to request support from any one of the numerous Warlord clans, for the best laid plans require large amounts of fodder.

A Master Moulder can't stop tinkering and adjusting the fleshy creations he has grown in vats, bred, and stitched together. A dozen failed grafts and self-maiming organisms are well worth any breakthrough in the creation of these hulks.
Skaven bodies are so numerous that a savvy Warlord would do well to sift through the chaff and pick out which rats to be equipped and which to serve as target practice.
Unholy amalgams of Moulder fleshcraft and Skryre techno-sorcery, these hulking abominations bear grafts that spew vile, burning ooze.

Displays of tactical acumen, anticipation of treachery, or simply unquestioning brutality are lavishly praised and rewarded by more cunning leaders, who grant access to armaments otherwise inaccessible to lower-ranking warriors.
They can be a powerful ally in the battle to come... or your Underling can earn some currency by fulfilling an assassination contract for the rat's head.

As an entire unlucky regiment of the verminous horde is engulfed in what can best be described as "ravening hellfire", you pray to the Horned One that this sabotage – *surely* it was sabotage! – took the miserable backstabbers with it.
The undulating, writhing mass of limbs collapses upon an unfortunate pack of vermin, their last screeches mingling with the loathsome sounds of the abomination's gorging.

Thinking themselves exceptionally clever, these unfortunate miscreants have gorged on contaminated supplies meant for surface world sabotage and now seem to be bleeding from every imaginable orifice, screeching an unholy racket in what are surely their death throes.
In Skryre, talent means surviving your own devices and others’ envy. Prove unscrupulous enough, and the whole ladder bends under your claws.

While the Skaven thrive amongst softer races and climates, a perilous assignment for the Council in the Chaos-ridden northern reaches – one he was not at all expected to return from – has hardened the resolve and deepened the malice of this specimen.
It serves the Skaven well that, even when faced with irrefutable evidence, many fools deny the existence of bipedal ratmen.
A dozing guard-thing is the first favourable omen of the raid. Slit his throat and eat him quick-quick, to ensure good fortune.
Know one Skaven secret, and you hold his tail. Know two, and you seize his scruff. Know three, and your claw is at his throat.\\n– Skaven proverb
During tunnel extension, a stockpile of Dwarf-made barrels was found – perhaps it should be furtively moved to the guardhouse mess hall, tempting their drunken revelry?
The ale-trap bears fruit – our agents will have an easier time sneaking past bloodshot eyes and hiccup-ridden mumbling!
A rare and unfortunate circumstance – these solemn beard-fools are resolute in their duty and refuse to drink!
Golden are these man-thing fields, yes-yes, and their posh tin-heads stare too long at bright banners to notice what scurries below.
If these vow-apes wish to keep their treasures, perhaps they should toss them in their precious Lady's lake. Surely she's more observant than their clank-clad guard!
For an "Iron" Dragon, the eastern lord-thing meddles too much with substances beyond his unrefined taste. Better for everyone to rid-strip him of precious supplies like these, lest they go to waste.
The fire-stunties must share the wit of the horned animal-god they so fervently worship, trusting chains and locks to guard the spoils of their slaving ways.
Daemon-things waste abundant warp-matter in mindless veneration of their squabbling, lesser gods. Skaven will put it to better use, yes-yes.
A lucky find! Or is it a trap in disguise, a plot by a rival Skaven to undermine the plan and embarrass the Underling?
The Greenskins are contemptible morons, whose unpredictable bloodthirst can be as much a detriment as it can be a blessing. Raid the stockpile quick-quick, before these lunatics return!

Warp-addled vermin speculate that the lineage of Skaven and Ogres can be traced to a common origin, for the flesh-craft of the two races is among the most successful of Moulder experiments, and they both share such uncanny, insatiable hunger...
These intractable lumpen-brutes pile their ill-got gains for some inevitable tribute to the gnaw-hole they call a god! Best redirect such resources to more discerning minds.

Most frustratingly, the withered dead-things seem largely unaffected by prolonged exposure to the god-stone and use it for their own wasteful, inscrutable ends! Strike during their dormancy and place it in rightful paws.
The Underling has somehow tunneled into a vault room – opening it carries risk of alerting the guards, but the riches that could be inside...
Your Underling has already started displacing the meat contents of multiple Corpse Carts, either lazily unguarded or left without the owning Necromancer.
Stumbling upon a location full of corpses, belonging to a well-prepared Necromancer or Vampire, your Underling believes that some meat can be salvaged from the bones.
Nought is more suspicious than an overly helpful agent of the Council. Exploit this servile schemer – but cut him loose-loose before the trap is sprung!
Strong Winds blowing from the north have been felt by the Underling – they can be used, but with some risk of drawing Daemonic influence.
The Underling attempts to use the arcane energies to suffuse the ritual with more power, dismissing the chance of magical complications.
Without utmost concentration, these prismatic things are a formless shimmer threading at the doorstep of the unseen.
A secret Skaven laboratory glows in the gloom. Feed it warpstone, silence the shrieks, and its horrors may yet serve your design.
A hidden Skaven regiment, planted for another scheme, has surfaced within reach. Steal its loyalty before its true master notices.
Scarred Stormvermin stand ready, their halberds nicked by old battles and their loyalty sharpened by ample payment.
A mercenary company of Ogres has been spotted – if we do not hire them, their hunger could lead them to our tunnels!
Pay the Ogres to have them join you for this {{tr:chaotic_plans_name_wh3_dlc29_military_plan}} battle – we don't know what exact troops they will send, but it will be Ogres!
The Underling is now the client of an Ogre mercenary company – they will be joined in battle!
Hulking and pleasingly obedient, these Rat Ogres resemble their surface namesakes only in appetite and the ruin they leave behind.
The bickering fools have agreed on a most prudent decision – to offer support to the Underling.
Skaven guards are still guards, however wretched. Distract them with threats from above, then strike from the tunnel beside them.
Black-furred killers have decided survival lies with you. Reward their wisdom, but keep enough blades at their backs.
Dry bones and rusted blades bar the path. They do not fear, hunger, or tire, which makes them deeply irritating guards.
Cackling Daemon-things split, shriek, and caper where discipline should stand. Such nonsense is dangerous!
Death Runners pick through the aftermath with blades already wet. Best recruit them before they decide you are the aftermath.
Nagash’s favoured dead cast long shadows. Even absent, their will leaves grave-cold discipline where your schemes must pass.
A practicioner of Dark Magic requires corpses for their experiments – perhaps some Skaven warriors can be spared for a deal?
The tree elf-things move with hateful grace, arrows ready at the twitch of a whisker. Perhaps simply burning the whole cursed weald is better than risking an arrow through the eye?
With growing fear, you realise this man-thing peers beyond the veil for hidden truths – not least, likely, your presence!
Spaced evenly around the oxen carts, battle-hardened veterans march in unnerving harmony, eyes set forward and blades ready.
Heedless sorcery has twisted these man-things' feeble forms, and filled the Daemon-eaten chasms of their souls with a craving for the profane.

This strange and tortured Dwarf-thing hobbles away from its hateful throng with considerable effort, hoarsely rumbling a chant along the way – an incantation that ushers in a most fearsome presence...
Brass chains clink beneath guttural barks as black-clad stunties circle their subjugated throng like carrion birds.
Surface finery cannot soften the cruelty etched upon this Elf-thing’s face – a grimace used to seeing all squirm beneath her penetrating gaze.
Thirteen curses be inflicted thirteen-fold upon the ginger-furred, one-eyed madman and his man-pet! How can they possibly meddle-spawn right in the midst of your perfect scheme?!
Muscle-bound and festooned with bone charms, the Greenskin rattles a skull and contorts his body in rhythmic mockery of conjuration – and, to your horror, something answers its call.
May the Horned Rat crack the pointy ears' precious island asunder for standing in your path, and usher the Great Ascendancy snout-first through their realms!
Your fur bristles of its own accord, as the air around these pointy-helms thrums with unnatural intensity.
Most fearsome, this man-thing: her sorcerous trickery turns the chittering tide into a sluggish morass of frosted fur.
None is more hated or feared by the Skaven than the bloated frog-wizards, for even in a sluggish state of near-torpor, they can visit untold devastation upon the sprawling webwork of the Underway.
Woefully crude even by man-thing standards, these addled Shaman-Sorcerers do not seem to mind proferring ratmen guts to their squabbling gods.
These festering dregs will surely be of interest to the plague priests, ever in search of new and greater maladies – but first they must be disposed of!
Were you forced to grant these brutes intellect, you would call them proudly competitive in the number and variety of skulls on their belts.
Ogres roam dangerously close to our tunnels – we could leave some food to sate them and ensure they do not get curious...
An Ogre consumes as much as a full warren of Skaven – but it may be worth it to keep the Ogres fed and sleepy.
Fed and drowzy, the Ogres are much less likely to cause complications for the Underling.
Wretched, dim-witted vermin stand in the way of your complex and interweaving schemes. Do they not know who you are?!
Triumph tastes Warpstone-sweet to an Underling with more ambition than cunning sloshing about in his hollow cranium! Reckless fool-fool!
Cold authority burns in this horror’s hollow sockets, while the dust of aeons shakes from its desiccated garb with every step.
Whether by sheer incompetence or some warding magic, the guards realised that the vault has been breached!
A terrible curse indeed, to cross paths with a knight-thing pledged in his wandering never to sleep two nights in the same place.
Their garb is patchy, their pitchforks pathetic, yet their zeal seems annoyingly feverish. Kill-silence them before they find courage.
Upon careful scrutiny, one might observe that the eastern man-things act in practised accord that is nearly... unsettling.
These conniving dregs would hurl themselves upon your ranks in reckless frenzy, if only to stave off their wicked masters’ punishment.

A cloak of dull vermilion drips lavishly across razor-sharp epaulettes and neatly obscures an immaculately woven chainmail. Yet it does nothing to disguise the most wickedly scarred Elf-thing you have ever laid eyes on!
Eyes of depthless cruelty sweep the perimeter, while blades of exquisite craftsmanship gleam wickedly in the moonlight.
Why must every Orc-thing rear its ugly mug on your triumphant path? Could their Warboss not call them to a Waaagh! elsewhere?!
The knife-eared host’s garish white garb is almost as unpleasant as their sheer number.
Brass-bound killers prowl nearby, frothing for skulls and slaughter. Direct their frenzy elsewhere before they mistake rat-flesh for worthy tribute.
None of the furs cloaking these grim-faced man-things belongs to Skaven, and yet they set your nerves ill at ease.
Heavy boots, heavier guns, and colder eyes than any proper man-thing should possess! Avoid their line of fire, then strike from beneath.
The bloated frog-wizard barely stirs, yet its cold awareness presses upon the Underway. Move fast before its venerable instincts become action!
Crests flash in silent warning as scrawny lizard-things scrutinise the perimeter with glassy, unblinking intensity.
Reeking northmen stalk the wilds, drunk on ruin and blood. Best not attract their feral gaze...
A tallyman of rot has turned its sunken gaze this way. Every laboured step brings swarming flies and the scrutiny of its rheumy eyes.
Observing these feral flesh-things’ contemptible manners, you briefly question what surface-dwellers see in this particular pseudo-deity.
With the lurching dead, one key advantage of a sudden Skaven raid – instinctive revulsion and fear – is sadly negated.
A young Vampire has decided to use our tunnels for combat training – the Underling should form a skirmish group to deal with them!
A Strigoi Vampire has decided to prey on our tunnels and chew through our ranks – the Underling should form a skirmish group to deal with them!
The leaves rustle at your movements and branches snap beneath your paws with an intensity twice their due. Could the wood itself be helping guard this dung-heap?
Secure Clan Eshin's aid, and shadow-blades will stalk the final battlefield, slitting throats around the Morskittar Engine.
Buy Clan Mors' strength, and hard-bitten warriors will hold the line with brutal discipline around the Morskittar Engine.
Pay Clan Moulder, and stitched horrors from Hell Pit will be loosed in defence of the Morskittar Engine.
Appease Clan Pestilens, and diseased zealots will bring contagion and dreadful devotion to the final defence.
Purchase Clan Rictus' loyalty, and black-furred killers will anchor the Morskittar Engine’s defence with grim efficiency.
Fund Clan Skryre, and the final battle will blaze with weaponry only slightly more dangerous to the foe than to its operators.
Fold distance beneath claw and horn, hurling a Daemon Lord where its arrival will cause the most useful terror.
